newsitem.title: UK: Plantation urges vote against MD removal.
newsitem.headline: Plantation urges vote against MD removal.

text.p: Plantation & General Investments Plc said on Thursday it had written to shareholders urging them to vote against a resolution by Nicholas Roditi calling for the removal of managing director Konrad Legg.

Plantation, which owns and operates tea, coffee, rubber and other plantations overseas, said in the letter: "It is clear from Roditi's actions that he is attempting to gain control of the company without making a full offer at a fair price".

Roditi, an international fund manager who is reported to manage funds on behalf of financier and investor George Soros, also seeks to appoint Rupert Pennant-Rea, ex-deputy governor of the Bank of England, and Derek Netherton to the board.

"Roditi's keen interest in removing the managing director and his efforts to install Pennant-Rea and Netherton are an opportunistic attempt to seize control of a company whose trading performance is on the upturn," Plantation said in the letter.

In February this year Roditi, through Rovida International Ltd -- a company controlled by him and of which Netherton is a director -- said he was considering making an offer for Plantation entire issued share capital at around 58 pence per share.
Plantation was and continues to view the offer as not representing fair value for shareholders.

"Having failed to gain a recommendation by the board of a low offer price earlier in the year, Roditi has now selected another route to obtain control of Plantation," chairman Selwyn Pryor said in a statement.
"I urge shareholders to vote against this resolution and frustrate his attempt to remove the company's managing director".
The group's annual general meeting, which will consider the resolution, is to be held on July 31.
